scope: Kirinyaga, Machakos, and Nakuru horticulture opportunity assessments

records.source_name: Wang'uru & Wakulima Wholesale Market Price Bulletin
records.title: Kirinyaga tomato wholesale prices by seasonal window
records.claim: Wholesale tomato prices in Wang'uru market averaged 78-95 KES/kg during dry season (July-Sept) but dropped to 42-55 KES/kg during peak rain glut.
records.detail: Survey of wholesale buyers across Wang'uru and Nairobi Wakulima markets shows Grade 1 Anna F1 and Kilele F1 tomatoes fetched 85 KES/kg median in dry harvest. Peak harvest in Mwea creates 40% price deflation without cold-chain storage.
quality_flags: Wholesale price varies by grade; transport costs to Nairobi Wakulima (~12 KES/crate) must be accounted for.

records.title: Open-market price volatility and payment terms
records.claim: Middlemen and informal aggregators in Wang'uru pay cash on delivery but enforce a 15-20% rejection rate on uncalibrated crates.
records.detail: Without a formal offtake agreement, smallholders selling at farmgate absorb rejection costs and lack price protection during harvest surges.
quality_flags: Rejection criteria depend on grading calibration.

records.source_name: KALRO Horticulture Research Institute - Production Budget
records.title: One-acre hybrid tomato production cost breakdown
records.claim: Total production cost for 1 acre of open-field hybrid tomatoes (Anna F1 / Kilele) is approximately 195,000 to 240,000 KES.
records.detail: Breakdown per acre: certified seeds (18,000 KES), seedling nursery propagation (12,000 KES), land preparation & ridging (20,000 KES), basal & topdressing fertilizer (45,000 KES), pest/disease chemical spray program (38,000 KES), trellising stakes & twine (32,000 KES), labor & harvesting (40,000 KES). Yield potential under good management: 18-25 tons/acre.
quality_flags: Yield is contingent on pest management (Tuta absoluta, bacterial wilt) and reliable irrigation.

records.source_name: Water Resources Authority (WRA) Mt. Kenya Sub-Region
records.title: River Thiba & Nyamindi seasonal abstraction quotas
records.claim: Unregulated furrow water abstraction is prohibited during dry months; drip irrigation with permitted storage weir is mandatory.
records.detail: Dry-season farming requires an on-farm water reservoir (min. 150m3) or shallow borehole. Pumping fuel costs add 22,000-30,000 KES per cycle if grid electricity is unavailable.
quality_flags: Permit application lead time is 4-6 weeks.

records.title: French beans export contract pricing in Machakos / Yatta
records.claim: Export packhouses offer contract pricing of 95-120 KES/kg for extra-fine French beans meeting GlobalGAP compliance.
records.detail: Fixed-price contract agreements protect growers against local market price collapses, but non-compliant batches with MRL (Maximum Residue Limit) exceedances are rejected at the packhouse gate without compensation.
quality_flags: Requires strict spray diary record-keeping and GlobalGAP certification.

records.title: Yatta canal water rotational rationing
records.claim: Canal maintenance and low river intake cause 2-day-per-week water shutdowns during dry periods.
records.detail: Growers reliant exclusively on direct canal tapping without buffer storage suffer blossom drop and pod curvature, reducing export grade pack-out from 80% to below 45%.
quality_flags: Buffer water pan required for continuous drip.

records.source_name: National Potato Council of Kenya (NPCK) Market Watch
records.title: Nakuru & Molo Irish potato wholesale bag prices
records.claim: A 50kg bag of Shangi variety wholesale in Nakuru traded at 2,400-3,200 KES (48-64 KES/kg) during off-season.
records.detail: Commercial production in Molo and Mau Narok yields 80-120 bags/acre. Seed tuber cost (certified Shangi at 3,800 KES/bag, 12-14 bags required per acre) accounts for nearly 40% of initial operating capital.
quality_flags: Seed tuber quality directly dictates bacterial wilt incidence.

records.source_name: Kenya Meteorological Department - Rift Valley Agrometeorology
records.title: Nakuru highland frost and rainfall cessation outlook
records.claim: Highland frost events in late November and unpredictable rainfall cessation pose risks to late-planted tubers.
records.detail: Cold-tolerant varieties and early-October planting mitigate frost damage; unseasonal rains during harvest double post-harvest rot losses in ambient on-farm storage.
